hints: Use integration by parts with the algebraic factor as the part to differentiate.
Integrate $\cos 3x$ carefully, including the factor from its argument.
Complete the remaining sine integral to obtain an antiderivative containing $x\sin3x$ and $\cos3x$.
Apply the limits $0$ and $\pi/6$ exactly, then combine the rational and $\pi$ terms.
walkthrough:
Apply integration by parts $\int u\,\mathrm{d}v = uv - \int v\,\mathrm{d}u$ to $\int_0^{\frac{1}{6}\pi} x\cos 3x\,\mathrm{d}x$:
$$u = x \implies \mathrm{d}u = \mathrm{d}x$$
$$\mathrm{d}v = \cos 3x\,\mathrm{d}x \implies v = \dfrac{1}{3}\sin 3x$$

Evaluate at the upper limit $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$:
$$3\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$$
$$\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 1, \quad \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0$$
$$\text{Upper value} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)(1) + \dfrac{1}{9}(0) = \dfrac{\pi}{18}$$

Evaluate at the lower limit $x = 0$:
$$\sin(0) = 0, \quad \cos(0) = 1$$
$$\text{Lower value} = \dfrac{1}{3}(0)(0) + \dfrac{1}{9}(1) = \dfrac{1}{9}$$

Subtract the lower limit value from the upper limit value:
$$\int_0^{\frac{1}{6}\pi} x\cos 3x\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{\pi}{18} - \dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{\pi - 2}{18} = \dfrac{1}{18}(\pi - 2)$$
